scope_warning: The graph is a deliberately broad seed, not all companies, experts, products, innovations, countries, subindustries, or practices.

gaps.description: Most company capability surfaces are verified only from official documentation; comparative effectiveness, failed deployments, total cost, exitability, and outcome magnitude are not independently established.
Acquisitions, product retirements, parent ownership, and brand continuity can change rapidly; every company needs a periodic legal/currentness pass.
next_evidence: official corporate registry or investor filing

gaps.description: Pricing units, minimum commitments, data egress, model export, contract termination, and supplier-exit behavior are rarely public and remain unmodeled for most companies.
The upstream analytical-practice registry lacks explicit discrete-choice modeling and multiple-imputation practice records, so expert mappings cannot yet resolve to correct horizontal practice IDs.
next_evidence: adjudicate overlap with causal and uncertainty contexts

gaps.description: The corpus now includes artifact-attributed contributors for MetricFlow, OpenLineage, Great Expectations/GX Core, and SodaCL, but data-contract standards, observability detection/incident methods, and additional semantic-layer implementations still need contributor-level research that separates authorship from company leadership.
next_evidence: maintainer histories for data-contract and observability artifacts
independent technical talks tied to shipped artifacts

gaps.description: The seed is biased toward English-language and globally visible vendors; specialists in Latin America, Africa, Middle East, Central/Eastern Europe, East/Southeast Asia, and local regulated markets are underrepresented.

Healthcare, finance, energy, telecom, industrial, retail, and supply-chain seeds are present, but agriculture, mining-specific geology, aviation revenue/operations, maritime, defense, public finance, education, water, climate, construction, and many subindustries remain incomplete.
next_evidence: cross-link every industry analytical case to candidate specialist providers
require at least two provider alternatives plus build/open-source option

gaps.description: The dated innovation list covers selected foundational interfaces/standards/engines, not every algorithmic, product, or domain innovation from 2021-08-25 through 2026-08-25.
next_evidence: systematic release-note pass per analytical family

gaps.description: No universal solver-performance claim is admitted. Problem classes, formulation, hardware, tolerances, version, time budget, and benchmark selection can reverse comparisons.
next_evidence: performance profiles with censored timeout handling

gaps.description: Named products/modules are evidence leads; most still require decomposition into bounded contexts, ports, policy decisions, state machines, provider requirements, and compiler-bindable capabilities.
AI-heavy companies frequently blend deterministic analytics with LLM/agent interfaces in the same product page. The current separation is cautious but needs feature-level dependency tracing.

No finite list can be 'all experts.' Records are selected because a cited artifact or exact contribution is reusable by the corpus; many researchers, maintainers, practitioners, and critics remain absent.
next_evidence: citation and standards networks used only for discovery

company_purity: analytics consultancies whose current identity is predominantly AI services
duplicate_or_overlap: forecasting product versus supply-chain planning suite
evidence_conflicts: outcome percentages without denominator or counterfactual
